main_text.l: Hac tamen, ô Blasi, de tempestate quietis Pacificæ, clades heu deploranda sequetur: Et graue manabit dulci de melle venenum. Vox est blanda quies, pax delectabile nomen. Plura tamen de pace fluent, opprobria, damna, Dedecora, ærumnæ: quàm de crudelibus armis. Degenerabit enim virtus antiqua, voluptas Inter opes & delicias delumbia reddet Corpora: et amittet mens eneruata vigorem, O studia, ô mores, ô tempora sordida. Cerno Oblitos Christum populos, incredula corda, Conculcare fidem, scelus omne incurrere facto Agmine certatim, fieriq; animantia bruta, Et Romam in caulas, atq; in magalia versam.

Cælicolæ, in gentes malè tunc animabimur illas, Atq; sua superi, quando impia sæcula cernent: Destituent ope terrigenas, caua tartara olentes, Irascente Deo, coitum mala sidera in unum Conuenient, tristes in humum iaculantia flammas. Atq; viam cœlum inveniet[?], qua conterat illud Infidum crudumq; genus. Solventur ab Arcto Terribiles hominum vultus, animiq; feroces: Sauromatæ, sine diuina sine lege humana Viventes, Hunni, Alani, Turci, atq; Agathirsi.

page.notes: Underlining in ink runs under the lines from "Hac tamen" to "armis" and under "Degenerabit"; these are pen marks, not print, and are not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "inveniet" (the scan looks like "mueniet", marked [?]); "delumbia" as printed; "Hac tamen" may be "Hactamen" in the print. The long s is read as s, and "fordida" is taken as "sordida" with a long s that looks like f. The left-hand brace is not text.
